title: The box model: content, padding, border, margin
why_it_matters: Every spacing bug starts with these four layers.
explanation: Every element is a box with four layers. Content sits in the middle, then padding, then the border, then margin outside. Padding is inside the border and shows the background, while margin is empty space between boxes.
try_it: Inspect any element in DevTools and hover the box diagram to see each layer.

title: box-sizing: border-box makes widths honest
why_it_matters: A 300px box stays 300px even with padding.
explanation: By default, width only sets the content size, and padding and border are added on top. With box-sizing: border-box, width includes padding and border. A box with width: 300px is then exactly 300px wide.
try_it: Add padding to a fixed-width box with and without border-box and compare the real width.

title: Before vs after: the border-box reset
why_it_matters: One rule makes sizing predictable across your whole site.
explanation: Many developers apply border-box to every element at the top of their stylesheet. Including the pseudo-elements means ::before and ::after behave the same way. Then widths mean what they say everywhere.
try_it: Add this reset to the top of your stylesheet and check that no layout breaks.

title: Common mistake: width 100% plus padding
why_it_matters: It fixes inputs that stick out of their container.
explanation: With the default content-box sizing, width: 100% plus padding makes the element wider than its parent, causing a horizontal scrollbar. Use box-sizing: border-box so the padding fits inside the 100%.
try_it: Make a full-width input with padding and check for sideways scrolling.

title: Vertical margins collapse together
why_it_matters: It explains why spacing between blocks seems too small.
explanation: When two block elements touch vertically, their margins merge into one instead of adding up. The merged gap equals the larger margin. This only happens vertically, never with left and right margins.
try_it: Measure the gap between this heading and paragraph in DevTools.

title: Quiz: what is the gap after margin collapse?
why_it_matters: It tests whether you really understand collapsing.
explanation: Question: a heading has margin-bottom: 30px and the paragraph below has margin-top: 20px. How big is the gap? Answer: 30px, not 50px. Touching vertical margins collapse to the larger value.
try_it: Wrap them in a flex column and see the gap grow to 50px, because flex items do not collapse.

title: position: relative sets a reference point
why_it_matters: It anchors children that you place with absolute.
explanation: position: relative keeps an element in the normal flow, and lets you nudge it with top, left and similar. Its main job is to become the reference point for absolutely positioned children inside it.
try_it: Pin a small badge to the top right corner of a card.

title: absolute positions against a parent
why_it_matters: You know exactly where the element lands.
explanation: An absolutely positioned element leaves the normal flow and is placed relative to its nearest ancestor that has a position other than static. It no longer takes up space, so siblings move into its place.
try_it: Cover a card with a semi-transparent overlay using inset: 0.

title: Common mistake: absolute child flies off
why_it_matters: It stops a badge from landing in the page corner.
explanation: If no ancestor is positioned, an absolute element uses the page as its reference and jumps to the page corner. The fix is to add position: relative to the parent that should hold the element.
try_it: Remove position: relative from a card and watch the badge leave it.

title: position: sticky keeps headers in view
why_it_matters: A header or table heading follows the reader.
explanation: A sticky element scrolls normally until it reaches the offset you set, then it sticks in place. You must give it a top, bottom, left or right value, otherwise nothing happens.
try_it: Make a navigation bar stick to the top while the page scrolls.

title: Common mistake: sticky that never sticks
why_it_matters: It saves you an hour of guessing.
explanation: Sticky usually fails for two reasons. A parent has overflow set to hidden, auto or scroll, which becomes its scroll area, or the parent is exactly as tall as the sticky element, leaving no room to move.
try_it: Check every ancestor of a stuck-less sticky element for an overflow value.

title: position: fixed stays on screen
why_it_matters: It is how floating buttons and bars are built.
explanation: A fixed element is positioned against the viewport and does not move when you scroll. It leaves the normal flow, so add padding to the page content to stop the fixed bar covering anything.
try_it: Add a fixed help button in the bottom right corner of a page.

title: z-index needs a positioned element
why_it_matters: It explains why z-index sometimes does nothing.
explanation: z-index only works on elements with a position other than static, and on flex or grid items. Setting z-index: 10 on a plain block does nothing. Add position: relative first.
try_it: Put a menu over another element and make z-index work by adding position: relative.

title: Stacking contexts trap your z-index
why_it_matters: It explains why z-index: 9999 still loses.
explanation: Some properties, like a transform, an opacity below 1 or a positioned element with z-index, create a stacking context. Children can only compete inside it, so a huge z-index inside a low context cannot beat a sibling above.
try_it: Find a popup hidden under another element and check its ancestors for a stacking context.

title: isolation: isolate creates a safe context
why_it_matters: A component keeps its z-index values to itself.
explanation: Adding isolation: isolate to a component creates a stacking context without needing position or z-index. Any z-index inside it then stays inside, so it cannot fight with the rest of the page.
try_it: Add isolation: isolate to a card that has absolutely positioned children.

title: Debug the box model in DevTools
why_it_matters: You see margin, padding and size at once.
explanation: Select an element in DevTools and open the Computed tab to see the box model diagram with exact values. Hovering an element also highlights margin in orange and padding in green, which makes spacing problems easy to spot.
try_it: Pick any element, read its box diagram, then edit its padding live.

title: Myth: overflow: hidden only hides things
why_it_matters: It has side effects that can break your layout.
explanation: Myth: overflow: hidden only clips what spills out. It also makes the element a scroll container, which can break position: sticky on its children, and it makes the box contain its floated children.
try_it: Use overflow: auto on a 200px tall box with long text and watch the scrollbar appear.

title: rem and em are relative sizes
why_it_matters: Your layout respects a user's font size choice.
explanation: rem is relative to the root font size, which is 16px by default. em is relative to the current element's font size. Use rem for consistent spacing and font sizes, and em when a size should scale with its text.
try_it: Change the browser's default font size and see which of your sizes follow it.

title: Quiz: how many pixels is 1rem?
why_it_matters: It tells you how rem actually scales.
explanation: Question: how many pixels is 1rem? Answer: it depends on the root font size, which is 16px in most browsers by default. If a user raises their default font size, every rem value grows with it.
try_it: Set html { font-size: 50% } and see what 1rem becomes.

title: dvh fixes the mobile 100vh problem
why_it_matters: A full-screen section no longer hides behind browser bars.
explanation: On phones, 100vh can be taller than the visible area because the address bar takes space. The dvh unit follows the visible viewport as the bar shows and hides, so min-height: 100dvh fits the real screen.
try_it: Open a full-screen hero on your phone and compare vh and dvh.

title: ch sets a readable line length
why_it_matters: Long lines are hard to read, and this limits them.
explanation: The ch unit is about the width of the zero character in the current font. A max-width of 60ch to 75ch keeps paragraphs at a comfortable length, whatever the font size is.
try_it: Limit a paragraph to 65ch and compare how it reads on a wide screen.

title: clamp(), min() and max() set sizes with limits
why_it_matters: One value adapts to the screen between two limits.
explanation: clamp(min, preferred, max) picks the preferred value but never goes below the minimum or above the maximum. min() takes the smaller of its values and max() takes the larger.
try_it: Make a container that is 90% wide but never narrower than 280px or wider than 960px.

title: Logical properties follow the writing direction
why_it_matters: Your spacing works in left-to-right and right-to-left.
explanation: Instead of left and right, logical properties use inline and block directions. margin-inline is left and right in English, but flips for right-to-left languages. padding-block means top and bottom.
try_it: Replace margin-left and margin-right in one rule with margin-inline.

title: Project idea: a modal with fixed and z-index
why_it_matters: It combines positioning and stacking in one build.
explanation: Build a modal dialog from scratch. Use a fixed overlay that covers the viewport, a centered box with a max-width, and a z-index so it sits above the page. Add a close button and test it on a phone.
try_it: List the three layers (page, overlay, modal) and decide their z-index values first.

title: Project idea: an article page with sticky nav
why_it_matters: It puts the box model, units and sticky to work.
explanation: Build a blog article page with a sticky header, a readable column limited with ch units, and comfortable spacing using rem. Add a sidebar table of contents that stays visible while the article scrolls.
try_it: Write a long article of lorem ipsum, then set its width to 65ch.
